entries.title: Psalms 129:1
segments:
. The people of God, often delivered from enemies, are confident of His favor, by their overthrow in the future. 
 
    1, 2. may Israel now say--or, "oh! let Israel say" (
). Israel's youth was the sojourn in Egypt (

entries.title: Psalms 129:2
segments: 2. prevailed--literally, "been able," that is, to accomplish their purpose against me (

entries.title: Psalms 129:3
segments: 3, 4. The ploughing is a figure of scourging, which most severe physical infliction aptly represents all kinds.

entries.title: Psalms 129:4
segments: 4. the cords--that is, which fasten the plough to the ox; and cutting denotes God's arresting the persecution;

entries.title: Psalms 129:5
segments: 5, 6. The ill-rooted roof grass, which withers before it grows up and procures for those gathering it no harvest blessing (
), sets forth the utter uselessness and the rejection of the wicked.
